newsitem.title: USA: Lower rates to boost Chile GDP 2nd half '97 - Garcia.
newsitem.headline: Lower rates to boost Chile GDP 2nd half '97 - Garcia.

text.p: Declining interest rates will propel Chile's economy toward swifter GDP growth in the second half of 1997, Economy Minister Alvaro Garcia said on Friday.
"We're expecting a 6.5- to 7.0-percent growth (rate) in the second semester," Garcia said at a U.S. Chamber of Commerce breakfast during a visit to Washington.
That compares with an official projection of five percent for the first half of the year and suggests an overall 1997 growth rate of between 5.5 and 6.0 percent, he said.

Chile has allowed its benchmark interest rate to fall to about 6.7 percent from 7.5 percent in recent months, prompting forecasts of faster growth, Garcia said. He added that rates should continue to decline slowly.
Earlier in the year, Chile maintained higher interest rates out of fears the economy was beginning to overheat.

"It was growing in the last couple years a tick below 8.0 percent a year, which would give us a higher rate than the one we can keep permanently," he said. "Although inflation was still going down, we felt that we needed to cool down the rate of growth."
Chile has enjoyed 13 years of uninterrupted economic expansion. In recent years, its growth rate averaged more than 7.0 percent.
Garcia projected a return to 7.0-percent annual growth rate in 1998, a rate he called "relatively permanent."
"Both exports and investment have grown faster than GDP, and that's the engine of growth in Chile," the economy minister said.
Evolving trade agreements and an improved domestic saving rate have made the economy more robust, he said.
